purpose: A 3D Slicer extension (OME-Zarr, Informatics) that reads and writes OME-Zarr/OME-NGFF multiscale images from local folders, .ozx archives, https:// and s3:// stores, loading the finest level that fits a memory budget, refining slice views at full resolution, and mapping labels, time series and OME-Zarr 0.6 scenes to Slicer volumes, label maps, segmentations, sequences and transforms. It targets microscopy and large-volume users who want to avoid converting to NRRD/NIfTI.
summary: Well-structured, documented extension (README, TUTORIAL, screenshots, CI, self-test) with MIT license and a catalog entry consistent with the CMake build (EXTENSION_DEPENDS "NA" matches empty build_dependencies; OMEZarr.py and its icon are installed). No concealed behavior, no telemetry, no eval/exec/pickle, no bundled binaries; network access is limited to user-supplied store URLs. The one environment concern is that `ngff-zarr[remote]>=0.52.0` is pip-installed into Slicer's Python on first use — with a confirmation dialog only when a main window exists and testing is off, so headless/scripted use installs silently. Remaining issues are minor (unbounded class-level cache, global length-unit change, QSettings instead of a parameter node).

safety.rationale: Read OMEZarr.py lines 1-2200: no eval/exec/pickle/subprocess/os.system, no telemetry, no credential harvesting; network use is urllib.request.urlopen on the user-supplied store URL (line 169) and ngff-zarr store access, which is the advertised function. S3 credentials are only read from the environment/settings and anonymous access is the default (lines 400-422).

environment.rationale: ensureNgffZarr (lines 382-397) pip-installs 'ngff-zarr[remote]>=0.52.0' into Slicer's Python on first use; it asks for confirmation only when a main window exists and testing is disabled, so headless or scripted loads install silently. No torch, no Qt/VTK-bundling packages, no import-time installation.

packaging.rationale: OMEZarr/CMakeLists.txt installs OMEZarr.py and Resources/Icons/OMEZarr.png via slicerMacroBuildScriptedModule; root CMakeLists sets EXTENSION_DEPENDS "NA", matching the catalog entry's empty build_dependencies; scm_url/scm_revision (main) and build_subdirectory "." are consistent. Only a 5 MB tutorial video is committed as a large binary.

license.rationale: LICENSE is MIT (Copyright (c) 2026 Fideus Labs LLC), permitting distribution; README line 140 points to it. The dependency ngff-zarr is not bundled but installed from PyPI at runtime, so its own license terms apply to that install.

soundness.rationale: Follows ScriptedLoadableModule structure, keeps heavy imports (ngff_zarr, psutil, vtk.util.numpy_support) inside functions, reports errors through userMessages, removes observers in AutoRefiner.stop, and offers progress/cancel. Minor issues: runResponsive pumps processEvents in a loop (re-entrancy), the class-level _multiscalesCache is never bounded, and settings live in QSettings rather than a parameter node.

utility.rationale: README (usage, feature list, limitations, development), TUTORIAL.md with eight screenshots, a walkthrough video, a GitHub Actions test workflow and Testing/run_headless_test.sh give a user a clear path; the module overlaps little with core Slicer readers, which do not handle OME-Zarr.

findings.title: ngff-zarr is pip-installed into Slicer's Python on first use, silently when no GUI confirmation is possible
findings.explanation: The dependency is installed into Slicer's shared Python environment the first time any OME-Zarr store is opened (including via slicer.util.loadNodeFromFile or drag-and-drop). When there is no main window or testing is enabled, `interactive` is false and pip_install runs with no confirmation at all, so a scripted or headless session modifies the shared environment without asking. In the GUI the confirmation is present, which is the acceptable path; the non-interactive path is the gap.
findings.suggestion: Refuse to install (and raise a clear error telling the user to install ngff-zarr) when no interactive confirmation is possible, or gate the silent install behind an explicit opt-in setting.

findings.title: Dependency requirement is a lower bound only; effect on Slicer-bundled packages not verifiable here
findings.explanation: The requirement is not an exact pin, which is good, but pip may still resolve transitive requirements that upgrade or downgrade packages Slicer bundles (numpy, dask, zarr). I could not inspect ngff-zarr's metadata from this environment, so whether a downgrade of a Slicer-bundled package can occur is unverified rather than established.
findings.suggestion: State in the README which packages ngff-zarr[remote] pulls in, and consider passing --no-deps or a constraints file if any bundled package can be replaced.

findings.title: Class-level multiscales cache is never bounded or invalidated on store change
findings.explanation: Every opened store (and every scene image, line 1053) is kept in a process-wide dict of lazy dask-backed multiscales for the lifetime of the Slicer session; clearCache() exists but I found no call to it in the code I read. Opening many large stores in one session accumulates metadata and open store handles.
findings.suggestion: Bound the cache (e.g. keep the last few stores) or clear it on scene close.

findings.title: Loading runs in a worker thread while the GUI thread pumps events
findings.evidence:
thread = threading.Thread(target=target, name="OMEZarr", daemon=True)
    thread.start()
    while thread.is_alive():
        slicer.app.processEvents()
findings.explanation: runResponsive keeps the UI responsive by calling processEvents in a loop, which lets the user trigger other actions (closing the scene, deleting nodes, starting another load) while a volume is being written into a preallocated VTK buffer. This is a pragmatic pattern rather than a defect, but re-entrancy during a load is not guarded.
findings.suggestion: Disable the module panel and the load actions while a load is in progress, or document the re-entrancy assumption.

findings.title: Display-units setting mutates the global application length unit node
findings.evidence:
unitNode = slicer.mrmlScene.GetNodeByID("vtkMRMLUnitNodeApplicationLength")
        if unitNode is None:
            return
        unitNode.SetDisplayCoefficient(1.0 / LENGTH_UNIT_TO_MM[lengthUnit])
        unitNode.SetSuffix(symbol)
findings.explanation: When the optional 'display units' setting is on, loading a store changes Slicer's application-wide length unit, which affects rulers and measurements in every module until resetDisplayUnits() is called. It is opt-in and reversible, so this is informational.
findings.suggestion: Mention in the setting's tooltip that it changes Slicer's global length unit for the session.

findings.title: Module state is kept in QSettings rather than a parameter node
findings.evidence:
class Settings:
    """QSettings keys. Values are read on each use so the module panel takes effect immediately."""
findings.explanation: Slicer convention is to store module state in a parameter node so it is saved with the scene and can be set from Python. Here the memory budget, orientation assumption, label/time options and storage options are global QSettings values, so they are not scene-specific and are not captured in a saved scene.
findings.suggestion: Consider a parameter node for per-scene options, keeping QSettings only for user preferences.

findings.title: 5 MB tutorial video committed to the repository
findings.evidence: **[Watch the walkthrough video](Screenshots/SlicerOMEZarr-tutorial.mp4)** (1 min, with captions), recorded on
findings.explanation: Screenshots/SlicerOMEZarr-tutorial.mp4 (about 5 MB) is committed rather than hosted externally. It is small enough not to break the build, but it grows the repository permanently and is not needed to build or run the extension.
findings.suggestion: Host the video externally (as the README already does for the user-attachments link on line 32) or keep it out of the source tree.

questions_for_author: When Slicer runs without a main window (scripted or headless use), ngff-zarr is installed into Slicer's Python without any confirmation. Would you make that path fail with an instruction instead of installing silently?
Does ngff-zarr[remote]>=0.52.0 ever resolve to versions of numpy, dask or zarr that differ from the ones Slicer bundles, and if so, is that acceptable to you?
Is `slicer.packaging.pip_check` available in the minimum Slicer version you target (5.12), or should the check fall back to importlib.metadata?
